top_level_objectives: Identify the structural components and 3D arrangement of the DNA double helix.
Explain the complementary base-pairing rules and the role of hydrogen bonding.
Recognize the antiparallel 5' to 3' directionality of complementary DNA strands.
Analyze the specific roles of helicase, SSB proteins, DNA polymerase, and ligase during replication.
Differentiate the continuous synthesis of the leading strand from the discontinuous synthesis of the lagging strand.
Explain the semiconservative model of DNA replication based on the final daughter molecules.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the overall 3D structure of DNA and its primary structural components (backbone vs. bases).
key_visuals: A large, rotating 3D DNA double helix situated in the center of the student's physical space.
Distinct visual textures contrasting the outer sugar-phosphate backbone with the inner steps (nitrogenous bases).
student_actions: Walk around the 3D model to observe the right-handed spiral of the helix.
Select the outer ribbons to highlight the sugar-phosphate backbone.
Select the inner steps to reveal the nitrogenous bases projecting inward.

scenes.brief_purpose: Examine the specific complementary base-pairing rules and the hydrogen bonds that hold the two strands together.
key_visuals: A magnified, highly detailed view of a few base pairs inside the helix.
Distinct colors and molecular shapes for Adenine (A), Thymine (T), Guanine (G), and Cytosine (C).
Visual representations of hydrogen bonds (two dotted lines for A-T, three dotted lines for G-C).
student_actions: Count the hydrogen bonds between an A-T pair and a G-C pair to observe the structural difference.
Drag and drop floating, unbound nitrogenous bases to pair them with their correct complementary match on a single strand.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate how the two strands run in opposite directions, establishing the 5' and 3' ends.
key_visuals: A flattened, ladder-like segment of DNA to clearly expose the terminal molecular structures.
Glowing labels indicating the 5' phosphate group and the 3' hydroxyl group at the ends of each strand.
student_actions: Trace the backbone of the left strand from the 5' end down to the 3' end using a hand gesture or controller.
Attempt to trace the opposite (right) strand from top to bottom, discovering and confirming it runs in the reverse 3' to 5' direction.

scenes.brief_purpose: Show the initiation of DNA replication, the unzipping of the helix, and the stabilization of single strands.
key_visuals: A long DNA molecule with a replication fork forming in the middle.
student_actions: Guide the Helicase enzyme along the center axis of the DNA to break the hydrogen bonds and 'unzip' the strands.
Place SSB proteins onto the newly exposed single strands to prevent them from immediately re-annealing.

scenes.brief_purpose: Illustrate continuous 5' to 3' DNA synthesis on the leading strand.
key_visuals: The replication fork with the 3' end of the new leading strand exposed.
A cloud of free floating deoxynucleotide triphosphates (dNTPs).
student_actions: Attach DNA Polymerase to the 3' end of the growing leading strand.
Hold a trigger/button to allow the polymerase to continuously add complementary nucleotides as it chases the replication fork.

scenes.brief_purpose: Explain discontinuous synthesis on the lagging strand due to the antiparallel nature of DNA.
key_visuals: The opposite side of the replication fork (the lagging strand template).
Multiple DNA Polymerase enzymes and pre-placed short RNA primers.
student_actions: Deploy DNA Polymerase to synthesize short stretches of DNA (Okazaki fragments) moving backward, away from the replication fork.
Repeat the deployment for a second Okazaki fragment as the fork opens wider.
Use DNA Ligase to seal the nicks between the adjacent Okazaki fragments, creating a continuous strand.

scenes.brief_purpose: Conclude the lab by showing the final products of replication and proving the process is semiconservative.
key_visuals: Two complete, identical DNA double helices floating side-by-side.
Color coding showing the original parental strands in a dark, opaque color and the newly synthesized strands in a bright, glowing color.
student_actions: Visually inspect both new molecules to confirm each contains exactly one parental (old) strand and one daughter (new) strand.
Interact with a final pop-up assessment panel to answer a question summarizing why this process is termed 'semiconservative'.
